note: who_can_notice is "unknown" unless an official help page or the builder’s own test accounts show what the other person sees; unknown is treated exactly like noticeable. notice_source quotes the official page. steps_followed is true only after the builder followed the steps on a test account.

entries.title: A device is signed in to your Google account
entries.what_it_means: Whoever has this device can open your Gmail, see where you have been, and change your settings.
entries.notice_why: The device is signed out of your account. Whoever uses it will notice the next time they open Gmail or another Google app.
evidence_first: Screenshot the device list, including this device's name, place and time.
steps: Then change your password, or they can sign back in.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Do not use this account for private messages until it is signed out. Talk to an advocate about when to do it.

entries.title: An app can use your Google account
entries.what_it_means: This app can see, and may be able to change, information in your Google account.
entries.notice_why: The app stops working with your account. Whoever set it up may notice if they use it.
evidence_first: Screenshot the app's name and what it has access to.
steps: Remove its access to your Google account.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Tell an advocate it is there.

notice_source.title: Google Account Help: Manage links between your Google Account and apps from other developers
notice_source.quote: If you remove access, the app can’t access your Google Account.

entries.title: An app can read your Gmail

entries.notice_why: The app stops getting your mail. Whoever reads your mail through it may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot the app's name and what it has access to.
steps: Remove its access to your Google account.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Use a new email account they do not know about for private messages.

steps: Remove its access to your Google account.

entries.title: A phone can reset your password
entries.what_it_means: Whoever has this number can use it to get into your account, even after you change your password.
entries.notice_why: Spare Key does not know whether Google tells the old number. Whoever has it would notice if they tried to use it.
evidence_first: Screenshot the recovery phone page. The last four digits are enough to show which number it is.
steps: If the number is not yours, change it to a number only you can reach, or remove it.
Google may still send codes to the old number for 7 days. Change your password and sign out other devices at the same time.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Tell an advocate, because this number could undo a password change.

sources.title: Google Account Help: Set up recovery options

entries.verified_how: Official help page checked for what the change does (Google Account Help: Set up recovery options); steps not yet followed on a test account

notice_source.title: Google Account Help: Set up recovery options
notice_source.quote: If you change your recovery info or other authentication factors, Google may send codes to your previous info for 7 days.

entries.what_they_see: Google may still send codes to the old number for 7 days after you change it. Whoever has that number could notice, and could still use a code in that time.

entries.title: Another email address can reset your password
entries.what_it_means: Whoever reads this email address can use it to get back into your account.
entries.notice_why: Spare Key does not know whether Google tells the old address. Whoever reads it would notice if they tried to use it.
evidence_first: Screenshot the recovery email page.
steps: Change it to an email only you can open, or take it off.
Google may still send codes to the old address for 7 days. Change your password and sign out other devices at the same time.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Tell an advocate, because this address could undo a password change.

entries.title: A phone or device can approve sign-ins
entries.what_it_means: A sign-in to your account can be approved from this phone or device.
entries.notice_why: That phone stops getting sign-in prompts for your account. Whoever has it may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot the 2-Step Verification page.
steps: Remove any phone, number or key that is not yours.
Make sure at least one way to sign in is yours, so you are not locked out.
Google may still send codes to the old phone for 7 days. Change your password at the same time.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Tell an advocate it is there.

entries.what_they_see: Google may still send codes to a removed sign-in phone for 7 days. Whoever has it could notice the prompts stop, or still get a code in that time.

entries.title: Your mail is being copied to another address
entries.what_it_means: Every new email you get is also sent to this address. Whoever reads it sees your mail.
entries.notice_why: Their copies of your new mail stop arriving. They may notice within a day.
evidence_first: Screenshot this settings page, including the address.
steps: Open Gmail settings, then Forwarding and POP/IMAP.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now. Tell an advocate it is there. Use a new email account they do not know about for private messages.

sources.title: Gmail Help: Automatically forward Gmail messages to another account

entries.verified_how: Source pages checked; steps not yet followed on a test account
entries.what_they_see: New mail stops going to their address. No official page says whether Gmail tells them, but they may notice the copies stop.

entries.title: A filter sends some of your mail to another address
entries.what_it_means: Mail that matches this filter is sent on to another address.
entries.notice_why: Those messages stop arriving for them. They may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot the filter, including what it matches and where it sends mail.
steps: Open Gmail settings, then Filters and Blocked Addresses.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Use a new email account they do not know about for private messages.

sources.title: Gmail Help: Create rules to filter your emails

entries.verified_how: Source pages checked; steps not yet followed on a test account
entries.what_they_see: The matching mail stops going to their address. No official page says whether Gmail tells them, but they may notice it stops.

entries.title: A filter hides some of your mail
entries.what_it_means: Mail that matches this filter skips your inbox or is deleted, so you may never see it.
entries.notice_why: Whoever set it up would only notice if they check your filters or expect you not to see those messages.
evidence_first: Screenshot the filter, including what it matches and what it does.
steps: Open Gmail settings, then Filters and Blocked Addresses.
Check All Mail and Trash for messages it hid.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Check All Mail and Trash for hidden messages when you can.

sources.title: Gmail Help: Create rules to filter your emails

entries.verified_how: Source pages checked; steps not yet followed on a test account
entries.what_they_see: The hidden mail starts reaching your inbox. No official page says whether anyone is told. Whoever set it up would notice only if they check your filters or your inbox.

entries.title: Someone else can open your Gmail
entries.what_it_means: This person can read, send and delete your mail.
entries.notice_why: Your account disappears from the accounts they can open. They may notice the next time they look.
evidence_first: Screenshot the Accounts and Import page, including this address.
steps: Open Gmail settings, then Accounts and Import.
Under Grant access to your account, select delete next to the address.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Use a new email account they do not know about for private messages.

entries.what_they_see: They can no longer open your mail. They will notice the next time they try. No official page says Gmail tells them.

notice_source.title: Gmail Help: Delegate and collaborate on email
notice_source.quote: To prevent ongoing access, either reset the account password, or remove the delegated user.

entries.title: Someone can see your location
entries.what_it_means: This person can see where you are right now.
entries.notice_why: You disappear from the people sharing with them, so they may notice quickly.
evidence_first: Screenshot the location sharing page, including who it is shared with and until when.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Talk to an advocate before you go anywhere you want to keep private, because they can see where you are.

entries.notice_why: The link stops working. Anyone using it may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot the location sharing page, including when the link ends.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Talk to an advocate before you go anywhere you want to keep private.

entries.what_they_see: The link stops showing where you are. No official page says whether anyone is told. Anyone who opens the link after that may notice.

entries.title: An extension can see what you do in Chrome
entries.what_it_means: This extension can read the pages you visit in this browser.
entries.notice_why: If someone uses this extension to watch you, what they see would stop.
evidence_first: Screenshot the extension's page in Chrome, including its name.
steps: If you did not add this extension, select Remove.
If it says it was installed by whoever manages this browser, you cannot remove it here. Use another device for private things, and tell an advocate.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now. Use another device for anything private, because this extension may see it.

sources.title: Chrome Web Store Help: Install and manage extensions

entries.verified_how: Source pages checked; steps not yet followed on a test account
entries.what_they_see: The extension stops running in this browser. No official page says whether anyone is told. If it was sending what it saw to someone, they may notice it stop.

entries.title: This browser sends your data to another account
entries.what_it_means: Chrome may be sending your history and saved passwords to an account that is not the one you checked.
entries.notice_why: Your history stops appearing in that account. Whoever uses it may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot Chrome's profile menu, showing which account it is signed in to.
steps: Turn off sync, or sign out of Chrome.
Change the passwords Chrome saved, from a device only you use.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now. Use another device for anything private, because what you do in this browser may be shared.

sources.title: Google Chrome Help: Sign in to Chrome

entries.verified_how: Source pages checked; steps not yet followed on a test account
entries.what_they_see: This browser stops saving to that account. No official page says whether anyone is told. Whoever uses that account may notice its history stop updating.

entries.title: Another adult shares your Amazon account
entries.what_it_means: They can see your orders and the addresses they go to.
entries.notice_why: They lose what you shared, so they may notice. Amazon says they must then wait 12 months to join another family.
evidence_first: Screenshot your Amazon Family page.
steps: If you joined their family, select Leave Amazon Family.
If you run it, select them. Then remove them from your Amazon Family.
Check where your recent orders went.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Avoid ordering anything to a new address from this account.

entries.title: A teen profile is on your Amazon account
entries.what_it_means: A teen in your household can shop from your account, and you approve their orders.

steps: Talk this one over with an advocate first, because it involves a child.
To take the profile off, select it. Then remove it from your Amazon Family.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now. Talk to an advocate about anything that involves a child.

entries.title: Someone else manages your Google family group
entries.what_it_means: A family manager can see some of what you do and change some of your settings.
entries.notice_why: You disappear from their family group, so they may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot your family group page, including who manages it.
steps: Select Leave family group, then Leave.
If your account is supervised, you cannot leave it yourself. Talk to an advocate.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now and screenshot it. Talk to an advocate about when to leave.

entries.title: Your photos are shared with someone
entries.what_it_means: New photos you take may be shared with this person, and photos can show where they were taken.
entries.notice_why: New photos stop arriving for them. They may notice.
evidence_first: Screenshot the partner sharing settings.
steps: Under Partner sharing, remove your partner.
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now. Avoid taking photos that show where you are, because they may be shared.

entries.what_they_see: They can no longer see the photos you shared. They will notice the next time they look at them.

entries.title: Someone can see your location in another app
entries.what_it_means: A person on this sharing screen can see where you are.
entries.notice_why: Most location apps show when someone stops sharing, so they may notice.
evidence_first: Keep the screenshot you checked.
steps: Open the app on your phone.
Find its sharing or circle settings.
Follow the app's guide on Safety Net (NNEDV).
entries.if_not_safe_yet: Leave it for now. Talk to an advocate before you go anywhere you want to keep private.

sources.title: Safety Net (NNEDV): Resources for survivors

entries.verified_how: Source page checked
entries.what_they_see: They can no longer see where you are in that app. Whether the app tells them depends on the app. Treat it as something they may notice.
